items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:

items.title: Can We Escape Metaphysical Skepticism? | Michael Tooley
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can we reason from what we directly experience to justified beliefs about what really exists?*

Michael Tooley explores whether direct acquaintance and logical probability can provide a path beyond metaphysical skepticism, while arguing that the skeptical challenge still deserves careful examination.

0:00 Starting Points Beyond Metaphysical Skepticism
1:58 Logical Probability as a Foundation
3:31 Equiprobability, Structure, and Learning From Evidence
9:35 The Limits of Inference to the Best Explanation
11:05 Induction Needs an Underpinning
13:03 From Sense Data to an External Reality

*Michael Tooley* is Emeritus Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder. He received a Boulder Faculty Assembly Excellence in Research Award in 1998 for his book _Time, Tense, and Causation,_ and is the author of the new book _Causation: A Defense of a Non-Reductionist Approach_ (Oxford, 2026).
